title: Compression
starter: A three-minute song is about 30 MB uncompressed, but under 3 MB as an MP3. Suggest what could have been removed, and what could not.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: Why compress?
facts: Smaller files use less storage space.
They transfer faster and use less bandwidth, so streaming and downloads work better.
More files fit on a device, and web pages load quicker.
stations.challenge: Give three reasons a website compresses its images.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Smaller files use less storage space.
Also credit: They transfer faster and use less bandwidth, so streaming and downloads work better.

questions.q: Why is data compressed? Select all that apply.
questions.a: To use less storage space; To transfer files more quickly; To use less bandwidth

questions.q: Which is a benefit of compression for a video streaming service?
questions.a: Video can be sent over slower connections without buffering

stations.name: Lossy compression
facts: Some data is permanently removed to make the file much smaller.
The removed detail is chosen to be hard for people to notice, such as sounds outside normal hearing.
The original file can never be recovered.
stations.challenge: Name two file types that use lossy compression.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Some data is permanently removed to make the file much smaller.
Also credit: The removed detail is chosen to be hard for people to notice, such as sounds outside normal hearing.

questions.q: What happens to the data in lossy compression?
questions.a: Some is permanently removed, so the original can't be restored

questions.q: Which file types typically use lossy compression?

stations.name: Lossless compression
facts: No data is lost: the file is rewritten more efficiently, and can be restored exactly.
Patterns and repeats are recorded once instead of many times.
The saving is smaller than with lossy compression.
stations.challenge: Why must a program file be compressed losslessly?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: No data is lost: the file is rewritten more efficiently, and can be restored exactly.
Also credit: Patterns and repeats are recorded once instead of many times.

questions.q: What is the key feature of lossless compression?
questions.a: The original file can be restored exactly

questions.q: Why must text and program files use lossless compression?
questions.a: Losing even one character or instruction would corrupt the file

stations.name: Which one, when?
facts: Photos, music and video: lossy is fine, and the saving is big.
Text, spreadsheets, program files and archives: lossless only.
Sometimes both: a video may use lossy video with lossless subtitles.
stations.challenge: Choose lossy or lossless for five file types, and justify each.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Photos, music and video: lossy is fine, and the saving is big.
Also credit: Text, spreadsheets, program files and archives: lossless only.

questions.q: Which type of compression should be used for each file?
questions.a: A photo on a web page = Lossy; A music streaming track = Lossy; A word-processed essay = Lossless; A program's installer = Lossless; A spreadsheet of results = Lossless; A video on a streaming service = Lossy

stations.name: Run-length encoding
facts: A lossless method: instead of storing every pixel, store the colour and how many times it repeats.
It works brilliantly on images with large blocks of one colour, and badly on noisy photos.
stations.challenge: Encode the first two lines of the image using run-length encoding.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A lossless method: instead of storing every pixel, store the colour and how many times it repeats.
Also credit: 001 1011 means eleven pixels of colour 001.

questions.q: Copy this image, then look at each row: how many runs does it have?
questions.a: The 8 × 8 image shown, at 1-bit colour depth (64 bits raw)

questions.q: A row of 8 pixels is 00001111. How would run-length encoding store it?
questions.a: Colour 0 four times, then colour 1 four times

stations.name: Does it always help?
facts: RLE shrinks images with long runs of the same colour.
On a detailed photo, where colours change every pixel, it can make the file bigger.
Compare the raw size with the compressed size to decide.
stations.challenge: Compare the raw data size and the compressed size for your image.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: RLE shrinks images with long runs of the same colour.
Also credit: On a detailed photo, where colours change every pixel, it can make the file bigger.

questions.q: When does run-length encoding work best?
questions.a: When the image has large areas of the same colour

questions.q: What happens if RLE is used on an image where every pixel differs from the next?
questions.a: The compressed file can be larger than the original

final.name: Final challenge: compress it

questions.q: Is each statement about lossy or lossless compression?
questions.a: Data is permanently removed = Lossy; The original file can be restored exactly = Lossless; Used for MP3 and JPEG files = Lossy; Used for text and program files = Lossless; Usually gives the smallest file = Lossy; Run-length encoding is an example = Lossless

questions.q: A 1-bit image row is 11111000. How many runs does run-length encoding need?
Why is compression especially important for streaming video?
questions.a: It reduces the bandwidth needed, so video plays without buffering

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: Give two reasons why files are compressed before being sent over a network.
points: Smaller files use less storage space.
More files fit on a device, and web pages load quicker.
Text, spreadsheets, program files and archives: lossless only.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 2.

exam.q: Compare lossy and lossless compression, using an example of a file that suits each.
points: The saving is smaller than with lossy compression.
Sometimes both: a video may use lossy video with lossless subtitles.
Photos, music and video: lossy is fine, and the saving is big.
Text, spreadsheets, program files and archives: lossless only.
A lossless method: instead of storing every pixel, store the colour and how many times it repeats.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 6.

exam.q: Explain why run-length encoding shrinks a cartoon image more than a photograph.
points: RLE shrinks images with long runs of the same colour.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 3.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
